title: Stratified validation harness and multi-signal de-escalation policy for Optimize
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and deliver a stratified validation harness plus a multi-signal de-escalation (graded rollback) policy for Optimize. The goal is to reduce blunt full-rollbacks by enabling graduated traffic reductions, targeted cohort pauses, and automated mitigation actions driven by a composite quality score. This ticket captures PRD-level requirements, acceptance criteria, A/B gating design, and a runbook for on-call escalation and manual override.
background: Current Optimize rollouts rely on single-threshold guardrails that trigger full rollbacks when a global metric crosses a limit. That approach causes unnecessary user impact for regressions concentrated in small cohorts or specific long-tail prompts. We need a more nuanced system that: (1) detects regressions across multiple signal families (quality, safety, latency, cost), (2) quantifies regressions in a regression budget, and (3) responds with graded mitigation actions (traffic capping, cohort pause, model variant fallback) before full rollback.
goals: Design a stratified prompt-cohort sampling matrix (by product, user tier, input-length, and semantic cohort) for continuous validation
Define a composite quality scoring function that weights multiple signals and produces a normalized 0-100 score
Specify a regression budget and mapping from budget consumption to mitigation actions (de-escalation policy)
Provide clear A/B acceptance criteria, statistical test choices, and minimum sample sizes for canary phases
Implement acceptance criteria and a verification plan so SRE/SE can run the rollout runbook in a fire-drill
non_goals: Rewrite Optimize evaluation tooling end-to-end (this ticket scopes to validation harness and policy definitions, not full infra implementation)
Define new model training procedures or data collection pipelines
Replace existing safety review process (this design should integrate with, not supplant, safety reviews)
requirements: Stratified sampling: support at least 6 cohort dimensions and ability to prioritize cohorts by traffic and business impact

Signals: ingest and normalize at least these families — semantic quality (BLEU/ROUGE alternatives and human-labeled checks), hallucination proxies, safety classifiers, latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens
Composite score: configurable weights per signal, ability to lock weights for paid customers
Regression budget: a configurable monthly budget expressed as allowable cumulative deviation (in composite-score units) before a full rollback is mandatory
De-escalation actions: defined tiers (alert-only, 10% traffic cap, 50% cohort pause, revert-to-variant) and automated enforcement hooks
A/B gating: pre-specified statistical tests (SPRT for small-effect detection, two-sided t-test for large cohorts) and minimum sample thresholds
Explainability: dashboard must show decomposition of composite score into signals, per-cohort contributions, and top offending prompt examples
Audit trail: every automated mitigation or manual override must create a traceable event with commit/PR links and decision rationale
acceptance_criteria: A stratified sampling manifest is created and validated against historical traffic for three pilot customers: enterprise, mid-market, and PLG
Composite scoring function is implemented in the Optimize evaluation pipeline and unit-tested with synthetic drifts (0-10 point shifts)
Regression budget is configurable in the Console and honored by the rollout engine in simulated runs
De-escalation policy executes the correct mitigation step for at least three synthetic regression scenarios (long-tail increase in hallucination, latency spike, safety classifier uptick)
A/B gating configuration prevents canary promotion when SPRT indicates support for the null at the defined alpha/beta thresholds
Dashboard shows real-time composite score, cohort breakouts, and exposes top 50 prompts contributing to regression
Runbook is documented and SRE/PM/SE complete a scheduled fire-drill with documented outcomes (ticket in ops-playbooks)
metrics_and_thresholds: Composite score baseline: 82-95 (normalized); degradation considered meaningful if delta >= 3 points
Regression budget: default 6 points-month (configurable per-customer); consuming >50% of budget triggers 'caution' mitigation

Tier mapping: caution (>=1.5 points delta) -> 10% traffic cap; escalate (>=3 points delta or 50% budget used) -> cohort pause; critical (>=6 points delta or 100% budget used) -> revert-to-variant/rollback
Latency SLO: p95 increase >25% over baseline triggers automatic latency-focused mitigation regardless of composite score
Safety sentinel: top-quantile sentinel failure count increase >30% triggers immediate cohort pause for affected cohorts
a_b_test_design: Canary windows: phase-1 (1% traffic, 24h), phase-2 (5% traffic, 72h), phase-3 (25% traffic, 7d)
Statistical tests: SPRT for small-sample high-sensitivity signals, two-sample bootstrap for non-parametric signal distributions
Stopping rules: configured alpha=0.05, beta=0.2 for primary quality signal; if inconclusive after phase-3, promote only if composite delta < 1 point
Cohort-level gating: allow independent promotion decisions per cohort (enterprise cohorts can be held back while PLG is promoted)
Traffic split automation: support gradual ramp with automatic backoff if any cohort's 'caution' threshold is reached
deescalation_playbook: Alert classification: automated system emits 'info/caution/escalate/critical' and tags affected cohorts and signals
Automated mitigation sequence: info -> annotate + alert; caution -> apply configured traffic cap; escalate -> pause affected cohorts + notify SE; critical -> auto-revert-to-variant and page on-call
Manual override: PM or SE can force promote/rollback via Console with justification field; every override is logged and requires post-mortem if it bypassed critical safeguards
Communication plan: auto-created Slack thread to #optimize-deploys with summary, top prompts, and remediation steps
Post-incident: update regression budget per-customer if model change patterns indicate new baseline drift characteristics
dependencies: ENG-41820 - rollout engine hooks for graded mitigation
ENG-44002 - cohort sampling API and historical traffic sampler
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Composite score tuning could mask localized catastrophic failures -> Mitigation: require per-signal sentinel pass for any automated promote
Risk: Small cohorts produce noisy signals and false positives -> Mitigation: use SPRT + minimum sample constraint and allow cohort holdbacks
Risk: Operators overuse manual overrides -> Mitigation: require justification and quota tracking for overrides; quarterly audit
implementation_notes: Start with a pilot implementation that wires the composite score into the existing Optimize evaluate pipeline and simulates mitigation actions. Use synthetic drift generators plus one live canary customer. Keep weights configurable in Console and document default weight rationale.
